# Signed affine rebates defeat the replicated-guard capacity obstruction

The nonnegative-field capacity theorem is sharp, but its obstruction does NOT extend to the true signed convex physical cone. An affine base field cancels every total-mass and covariance contribution and gives strict loss to a favorable complete active menu. An explicit convex-body path verifies the descent independently of a formal separator.

## 1. Setup and a favorable actual menu

Use the actual replicated-guard body of `candidate b4250d3425f93191`: n=3L, d=2, central regular triangle T of centroid0, guard centers c_i=(1-sigma)v_i, and reflected fibers

    K_(+-e_(i,r))=c_i+sigma T,
    sigma=1/4.

Its unique actual source is0; every active continuous normal is one of the three canonical vertex directions and every balanced menu has total response weight1/3 per direction. For each canonical cap choose its actual independent base tilts to capture all of its POSITIVE matching guards and miss the negative matching guards. All nonmatching guards are missed. These choices have strict saturation margins and constitute a complete balanced actual menu.

Let P_D be the perimeter of one guard. Take the normal-independent physical field

    Phi(z,x)=sum_(i,r) z_(i,r).                       (1)

It is globally affine, hence convex, but signed. It vanishes on the central fiber, equals1 on every positive guard, and equals-1 on every negative guard.

Its total boundary-field integral is zero: identical reflected fibers cancel pairwise. For the selected menu, only the matching canonical direction contributes on a positive guard, with response weight1/3, while the negative guard profile is zero. Therefore

    integral W Phi dS = (3L)(1/3)P_D = L P_D>0.       (2)

## 2. The COMPLETE covariance term cancels

Normalize a cap's continuous normal so Gamma(u)=1. The exact pure-width first-variation terms are

    D(Phi)=sum_z integral_(boundary K_z) Phi,
    J_u(Phi)=sum_z integral [u·(X-g_z)]^2 Phi,
    dot Gamma(u)=[D(Phi)-J_u(Phi)]/(2M).

Here g_z is the ordinary centroid of its actual fiber. In every reflected guard pair, the two continuous bodies and their centroids are identical, while Phi has opposite signs. Thus BOTH D(Phi) and EVERY J_u(Phi) vanish exactly. The central fiber contributes zero. Hence every cap's covariance-norm derivative vanishes, not merely its leading-order approximation as h tends to zero.

The exact group response is

    sum_j theta_j {B_j(Phi)+A_j[D(Phi)-J_(u_j)(Phi)]/(2M)}.

Its covariance part and normalized-volume comparison beta D vanish. The remaining response is precisely the positive quantity (2), for every positive width in the certified guard regime. Thus the complete signed stress detects strict improvement although the nonnegative capacity is below1/e.

Adding an arbitrarily small positive constant epsilon to (1) gives a globally affine field with positive total boundary integral epsilon times the total boundary area. Its full response tends to L P_D>0 as epsilon decreases to zero. Therefore the ratio of full response to positive total boundary integral is unbounded. There is no finite signed-field analogue of the nonnegative efficiency obstruction for this menu.

## 3. An explicit valid body path

Let r_T>0 be the inradius of the regular triangle T, and put kappa=1/r_T. For sufficiently small |t| define the perturbed reflected guards by

    K_+(t)=c_i+(sigma-kappa t)T,
    K_-(t)=c_i+(sigma+kappa t)T,

at bases+e_(i,r) and-e_(i,r), respectively, while keeping the central fiber T fixed. Their inward Euclidean facet speeds are+1 and-1, exactly (1).

Take the canonical convex hull of these prescribed fibers. Its base projection remains the unit crosspolytope, so the only sampled bases remain0 and+-e_(i,r), and the extreme fibers stay prescribed. Any convex combination of endpoint bases landing at0 has equal weights on the two signs of each axis. Each reflected pair has Minkowski average

    [K_+(t)+K_-(t)]/2=c_i+sigma T=D_i.

These average bodies lie in T. Consequently the actual central fiber of the new body is EXACTLY T, even though an expanded individual guard need not lie in T. This proves validity of the finite body path rather than assuming an arbitrary signed normal motion is realizable.

The total mixed mass is

    M(t)=V[1+6L sigma^2+6L kappa^2 t^2].              (3)

The actual pooled within-fiber covariance is Sigma_T times

    [1+6L sigma^4+36L sigma^2 kappa^2 t^2
                       +6L kappa^4 t^4]
      /[1+6L sigma^2+6L kappa^2 t^2].                (4)

Both (3) and (4) are even in t. Thus M'(0)=0 and the derivative of every actual covariance norm is zero. No between-fiber centroid term enters the pooled within-fiber covariance.

The previously selected three canonical caps retain their strict outside statuses for all small positive t. Their own T masses change only through the covariance width and hence have derivative zero at t=0. Each captures L shrinking guards. Their common test mass is

    Q_test(t)=q_h(Sigma(t))+L V(sigma-kappa t)^2,

so

    Q_test'(0)=-2L sigma kappa V=-L P_D<0.            (5)

The last identity is the elementary area/perimeter relation for a regular triangle of inradius sigma r_T.

These three canonical cap normals positively balance and span the plane. At any point of the central triangle, at least one of their through-point thresholds is at least its through-centroid threshold. Its cap mass is at most Q_test(t). Therefore the maximum depth over the whole central fiber is at most Q_test(t). Every extreme guard has depth at most its own volume, which remains strictly below Q_test(t) for small t. The actual global normalized deepest value consequently satisfies

    beta(C_t)<=Q_test(t)/M(t),
    beta(C_0)=Q_test(0)/M(0).

Equations (3),(5) give a strictly negative right derivative for this upper bound. Thus beta(C_t)<beta(C_0) for all sufficiently small t>0. This proves genuine descent of the ACTUAL smoothed constrained depth, with all source candidates and all covariance changes accounted for.

## 4. What this does and does not settle

The replicated guards are valid obstructions to nonnegative individual capacity but are not stationary for the signed physical cone. Their forced nonnegative guard cost can be rebated by expanding a reflected guard that the selected cap misses while shrinking the one it captures. Pairwise equality cancels the global normalization and covariance terms exactly.

This does not assert a universal signed individual theorem or a universal separator independent of the active-menu choice. The favorable menu is selected first and the affine rebate is built for that menu. With several deepest sources, other source groups may react with the opposite sign, and their adaptive separating weights must be retained.

# Signed affine rebates defeat the replicated-guard capacity obstruction

**Signed affine fields escape reflected guard obstructions**

In the replicated triangle-guard family and its certified positive-width pure outward-smoothed model, select the caps capturing the positive guard in each reflected pair and use the affine field given by the sum of the integer coordinates. Opposite identical fibers cancel the first total-mass and pooled-covariance variations, while every selected smoothed cap has negative first variation. Explicit opposite homotheties preserve the exact integer fibers and yield a strict decrease of the actual normalized outward-smoothed maximum. This is a concrete signed escape in that model; no zero-width limiting conclusion for ordinary halfspace depth is asserted here.

Scope limits: A concrete signed escape for this compatible guard geometry, not a universal existence theorem for signed directions.
